title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: For how many ordered pairs \((a,b)\) of integers does the polynomial \(x^3+ax^2+bx+6\) have \(3\) distinct integer roots?

solutions.text:
By Vieta, the three distinct integer roots multiply to \(-6.\) The sets of three distinct integers with product \(-6\) are \(\{1,2,-3\},\) \(\{1,-2,3\},\) \(\{-1,2,3\},\) \(\{-1,-2,-3\},\) and \(\{1,-1,6\}.\) Each set determines \(a=-(p+q+r)\) and \(b=pq+qr+rp,\) and all five give different pairs, so there are \(5\) ordered pairs \((a,b).\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: If the roots are integers \(p,q,r,\) then \(pqr=-6\)
List the sets of three distinct integers with product \(-6;\) each set gives one pair \((a,b)\)
